This advice is based on my own experience, which has worked pretty well for me. I have read that store-bought blueberries are highly treated with fungicides, and picked before they are fully ripe. There's a guy here on this channel that grew blueberries on a farm up in New England, perhaps he can give you better advice than I can.

Getting Your Plants

Buy some healthy blueberry plants - about $15 each for a 3-gallon pot. You need more than one for good cross pollination, try to get different varieties. You can start from seeds, but it will take several years to get to a fruiting stage.

Planting

Dig a hole for each plant about twice the size of the root-ball of the plant. Make sure the plants are within 6 feet of each other. Acidify the soil by mixing in granular ammonium sulfate or sulfur-coated urea. Blueberries do not uptake nitrates in soil, so you need ammonia based fertilizers. Mix in some compost into the soil and plant the plants in the hole as you would with any other transplant.

Care

Maintenance is pretty simple with blueberry bushes, unless you're growing commercially and need to maximize yield, etc. Set up a drip line to water the plants regularly. Mulch the soil around the plants with at least 3 inches of mulch, to keep it from drying out. Once or twice a year, fertilize with a balanced acidic fertilizer. After the first few years, you will need to start pruning annually.
